articleHeadline: Venom breaks the schistosome parasite's resistance.
articleSummary: Brazilian researchers from USP and Instituto Butantan tested venoms from eight Bothrops snakes (including jararaca and jararacussu) on Schistosoma mansoni, a major cause of schistosomiasis. articleHeadline: Mantoux Tuberculin Skin Test: Early Detection of Tuberculosis Through the Skin
articleSummary: Mantoux tuberculin skin test (TST) uses intradermal injection of 0.1 ml purified protein derivative (PPD) into the forearm to detect prior exposure to Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Induration thresholds: ≥5 mm is positive for HIV/AIDS, close contacts, and those with prior TB on X-ray; ≥10 mm for healthcare workers, diabetes or kidney failure, children under 4, and residents in high TB areas; ≥15 mm for those without known risk factors. articleHeadline: Can swimming spread chickenpox?
articleSummary: Public swimming pools raise infectious disease risk. An MDPI study links most waterborne infections to fecal contamination and inadequate disinfection; enteric viruses account for 48% of pool outbreaks, 40% of ponds/lakes, and 12% of fountains. Recently in Hanoi, four children swimming together contracted Adenovirus. Shared facilities, including changing rooms and water toys, can harbor pathogens. Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV) causes chickenpox and shingles. After chickenpox, VZV remains dormant in nerve ganglia and can reactivate as shingles with age, chronic disease, or stress. Shingles is not directly contagious, but vesicles containing VZV can transmit chickenpox to contacts. Incubation for chickenpox is 10–21 days; complications include bacterial infection, pneumonia, encephalitis, or sepsis. Varicella vaccine provides up to 98% protection; post-exposure vaccination within 3–5 days reduces risk, even after day 5. Vietnam offers three monovalent vaccines and an MMRV combination; shingles vaccine is advised for adults 50+ and 18+ with immunodeficiency.

articleHeadline: More and more people in China are contracting COVID-19? Advice: Stop eating the 'four items' to protect the lungs.
articleSummary: June 2026 in China recorded about 79,000 new COVID-19 cases with the positivity rate rising for four weeks; summer waves (June–August) are expected. Shanghai respiratory doctors say waning immunity, viral mutations every 3–6 months, and indoor air-conditioning contribute to transmission. Diet strongly influences lung defense against SARS-CoV-2: the British Journal of Nutrition cites Mendelian randomization showing diet affects susceptibility, hospitalization, and severity; a US study of over 96,000 adults links ultra-processed foods (>40% of intake) with 26% higher COPD mortality and 10% higher chronic respiratory disease mortality. Four food groups matter: 1) high-sugar foods/drinks—Syrian hamster data show worse infection outcomes with high-fat/high-sugar diets; 2) processed meats—higher red meat intake raises pneumonia risk via nitrite-induced lung damage; 3) fried foods/reheated oils—oil fumes and oxidants provoke lung inflammation; 4) excess dairy—prefer fermented/low-fat dairy. A Mediterranean-like pattern reduced severe COVID risk (OR 0.31) vs Western patterns.

articleHeadline: Chongqing infectious-disease expert Liu Min reminds: Pertussis is making a strong comeback; these are the key facts everyone should know.
articleSummary: Pertussis (Bordetella pertussis) is making a global comeback. In 2024 China reported 476,690 cases—about 12 times 2023 and 30 deaths—peaking April–July. Globally, WHO recorded 941,582 cases in 2024; the UK ≈15,000; the US ≈35,435; Japan 89,387 in 2025; WHO Europe ≈300,000. School-age children (6–17) accounted for over half of 2024–25 cases, with 5–9-year-olds rising, reflecting waning vaccine protection and strain variation. In China, macrolide resistance is severe: about 99.7% of isolates resistant to azithromycin; overall macrolide resistance ≈70–100%. Alternatives include TMP-SMX and fluoroquinolones. Early symptoms resemble a cold; paroxysmal cough with a high-pitched inspiratory “whoop” can cause apnea in infants. Vaccination remains key: schedules start at 2 months, with an 18-month booster and a 6-year booster switched to DTaP; maternal Tdap offers neonatal protection, and adults should check PT-IgG and discuss boosters with clinicians.

articleHeadline: Prevention of anthrax-like infections: Department of Health urges after a typhoon or heavy rain to avoid contact with soil or muddy water.
articleSummary: After typhoons or heavy rain in Hong Kong, the Centre for Health Protection urges high-risk groups—elderly and people with chronic illnesses—to avoid contact with soil or muddy water to reduce melioidosis risk. Melioidosis is caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei in soil and muddy water, which can spread more easily after storms. Hong Kong last year saw 21 melioidosis cases. In response to a 2022 Sham Shui Po cluster, CHP and the Water Supplies Department implemented preventive measures: installing high-efficiency air filters at reservoir ventilation openings, maintaining residual chlorine in drinking water, and continuous monitoring of chlorine levels in reservoirs and taps, together with health education and infection surveillance. So far, post-typhoon and post-rain monitoring shows no abnormal results, and drinking water quality remains within Hong Kong standards.

articleHeadline: Molecular epidemiology of human rhinovirus in coastal China: genotyping and epidemic trends in Daishan (2022-2023) - Virus Genes
articleSummary: HRV accounted for 7.57% of 1,255 throat-swab specimens from influenza-like illness (ILI) cases in Daishan, Zhejiang Province, collected Jan 2022–Dec 2023. Real-time PCR screened 14 common respiratory pathogens; HRV detected in 95 cases (7.57%), with overall respiratory pathogens positive in 682 cases (54.34%). Nested PCR amplified HRV VP4/VP2 regions and phylogenetic analyses identified three HRV genotypes across 25 serotypes: 15 HRV-A types, 5 HRV-B types, and 5 HRV-C types. HRV was a main contributor to respiratory infections in Daishan during 2022–2023, with HRV-A being the predominant genotype and concurrent circulation of HRV-A, -B, and -C. The study supports ongoing HRV surveillance to monitor epidemic trends and genotype diversity; infection sources were hospital-based ILI cases in Daishan. No details on imported/exported HRV cases were reported.

articleSummary: In central Sudan’s Al Jazira state, the Batana area experienced reports of sheep die-offs, but the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries says these reports were inaccurate. articleHeadline: "Dizziness and fatigue are the first symptoms of a new COVID variant because the virus attacks the intestines? - Check the Facts."
articleSummary: COVID-19 misinformation check: dizziness and fatigue are not proven as early, variant-specific symptoms, and there is no evidence that a new strain starts by attacking the intestinal lining. Dizziness can have many causes and is not a diagnostic sign of infection or neural damage. Some COVID-19 patients may have gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea), but these are not established as common initial features of a new variant. Long COVID—prolonged fatigue in some recovered patients—is acknowledged by WHO but does not affect all cases. Claims that eggs or milk intake prevents or mitigates COVID-19 lack scientific support. In Thailand, the dominant circulating lineage is JN.1; from Jan 1 to July 19, 2026, there were 27,333 cases and 3 deaths, mostly among the elderly, with a healthcare system able to cope. Public health measures include DMH: frequent handwashing, masking in crowded places, and ATK testing when symptomatic.

articleHeadline: 14 cases of Lassa fever detected in Nigeria in one week.
articleSummary: 14 Lassa fever cases were detected in Nigeria in one week, per the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC). The seven-day total follows 31 cases the previous week, underscoring ongoing transmission. This year, confirmed Lassa fever cases have been reported in 23 states and 113 local government areas, with 224 deaths. The year-to-date case fatality rate is 23.9%, up from 18.9% during the same period last year. Most cases occur among 21–30-year-olds. The National Lassa Fever Incident Management System is actively coordinating response. Nigeria declared a Lassa fever emergency on 23 January 2019. Lassa fever is present across several West African countries, including Mali, Togo, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone; it was first identified in Nigeria in 1969 in Borno State. Transmission occurs via contact with rodent excreta and can spread person-to-person, causing a hemorrhagic fever; authorities urge avoiding rodent contact.
